object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A collection of products being transported, identified by a unique shipment number. Also called a consignment.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a Shipment.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: An item in inventory identified by a SKU (stock keeping unit).

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: SKU
object_types.definition: The stock keeping unit that uniquely identifies a Product.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: A numeric count of units in a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity.

ambiguities.description: Shipment-Warehouse cardinality: The fact type 'Shipment is stored-in Warehouse' has both a minimum (at least 1) and maximum (at most 2) frequency constraint on the Shipment role. This correctly captures that each shipment goes to 1-2 warehouses. However, the inverse direction is unconstrained: Can multiple shipments be stored in the same warehouse? The transcript does not explicitly address this, so the cardinality from Warehouse to Shipment remains ambiguous.
